notes.text:
Only the ENTIRE qualified G331, B341 and E350 are incoming correctness grants. Their annotations, ledgers, actual-primary-model scope, all-support conventions, conductor rules and precise smooth specialization remain attached. All public and 165 private hashes occur in the current manifests; the remaining 33 frozen files were separately retained and checked. All fifteen ROOT377 literal units are exact primary-source substrings with matching literal sizes/hashes. All ten actual native265 FINAL texts differ from their expansions. Every complete expanded body occurs in the 60,670-byte whole proof and in the 649,388-byte TeX under the declared character encoding. All three entire grants occur literally in both large paper formats. These are observed identity facts, not proofs or fresh historical reading receipts.

Two actual defects were identified. Smolkin v3 printed page 11 proposes making k an L-module through a retraction from the perfection of k(t). An action extending the k-action would give a unital ring homomorphism L to End_k(k)=k, which cannot exist. In particular, letting t act as zero contradicts t times t^{-1}=1. A fresh inspection of the retained page confirms the wording. N4 replaces this step with faithful flatness.

The ROOT377 literal entries indexed 13 and 14 are incomplete despite their completeness labels. The first ends during HLS7.5(f), before its sum over basepoint-free divisors. The second ends before Conjecture8.4 and Question8.5. Their missing tails were read and separately captured from the retained published text. Setting7.1 requires regularity; Section8.3 states subadditivity as a conjecture. No mixed-characteristic envelope theorem follows.

notes.summary: On excellent reduced primary sections, raw C/D envelopes agree; continuity is exactly geometric recognition and greatest-minorant existence. Exact gauges and actual decreasing-net closure are proved.
notes.detailedSummary: The arguments use qualified G331, retain all supports, and do not assume increasing completion or nested-net flattening. Global continuous-envelope positivity subsequently gives bounded USC greatest minorants through one decreasing C-net.
notes.text:
Use entire qualified G331. Let X={v:v(a)=1}, retaining every prime support. C is the uniform geometric cone and D its completion by ONE decreasing C-net. Both are nonpositive and stable under addition, nonnegative scaling and finite maximum; negative constants belong.

For finite continuous f define p(f)=sup{h in D:h<=f}. Constants make it finite. If h_alpha decreases to h<=f, the directed open sets {h_alpha<f+epsilon} cover compact X. One index works everywhere, so h_alpha-epsilon is a C competitor at least h-epsilon. Thus the raw C and D suprema coincide; p(f) is LSC and below min(f,0).

If p(f) is continuous, finitely many continuous competitors combined by maximum approximate it uniformly from below, placing it in closed C. Conversely membership in D gives USC, hence continuity. Its USC regularization remains below f and zero. If that regularization belongs to D, it is a competitor and equals p(f). Thus continuity, positive regularization and existence of a greatest D minorant are equivalent. A maximal minorant is greatest because its maximum with every competitor remains admissible. Negative shifts prove ||p(f)-p(g)||<=||f-g||, without an unrestricted translation identity.

The factorial formula does not recognize positivity. Set J_k={r:v(r)>=-k f(v) for all v}. Valuation axioms make this an ideal; if f>=-M it contains a^ceil(kM), so is unit or primary. An integral-dependence equation, passed first to the support quotient field, excludes a uniquely least-valued leading term and proves integral closedness. J_k J_l subset J_{k+l} and J_k^l subset J_{kl}. Rational primary profiles are dense in C; small negative rational shifts preserve the obstacle constraint. Their ideals lie in J_k, so sufficiently divisible factorial profiles dominate them. Hence p(f)=sup_j[-v(J_{j!})/j!] on all supports, with no increasing-D inference.

Decreasing D-nets are closed by insertion. On a normal branch let u=inf_i u_i. If u vanishes somewhere, G331’s zero dichotomy makes every u_i zero. Otherwise a tail is bounded above by -c<0. For finite continuous F>u, compact strict covers select one u_i<F and then one continuous term g of its actual representation with g<F and g<-c/2. Choose b>0 sufficiently small that b||g||<min(F-g). Then (1-b)g lies strictly between u and F, including bottom points. Insertion into the minimum of two strict continuous majorants makes their family downward directed. USC and a Urysohn cutoff provide a test F>u with arbitrarily prescribed upper value at one point, so the family’s infimum is u. Reverse pointwise order gives ONE decreasing C-net. Apply this on finite normalization branches and use full-fibre G331 descent for general reduced germs.

Signed rational primary differences are uniformly dense in all continuous functions. The lattice identity is min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH). Constants come from a; primary truncations (r)+a^N distinguish min(v(r),N), including infinite coordinates. Compact lattice approximation gives density.

For another primary gauge b, d(v)=v(b) and 1/d are positive bounded continuous. T(v)=v/d(v) transports obstacles and functions by f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). This order isomorphism preserves raw suprema, cones and regularization, giving the exact one-factor envelope cocycle.

Once GLOBAL CE is proved, finite continuous majorants F of a bounded USC obstacle form a min-directed family with infimum f. Their envelopes form ONE decreasing C-net. Its infimum lies in D, is below f and dominates every D competitor. Extended nonpositive USC obstacles are treated similarly; bottom uses negative constants. Decreasing USC obstacle nets commute with envelopes by the proved decreasing-D closure. Local finite-Q continuity alone is insufficient. Dimension zero has the unique empty envelope.

notes.summary: Full relative regularity proof: coherent M is generated when H^i(M A^-i)=0 on finite-dimensional projective Y over a Noetherian affine base, with A ample and generated.
notes.detailedSummary: The Koszul proof requires no smoothness, flatness, Cohen–Macaulayness or field base. It replaces the unread relative-book proof rather than applying GJKM’s smooth theorem to singular models.
notes.text:
Let Y be projective over a Noetherian affine scheme, A ample and globally generated, M coherent, and d=dim Y finite. Assume H^i(Y,M tensor A^{-i})=0 for 1<=i<=d. Higher groups vanish by the ordinary coherent-cohomology dimension bound.

Choose finitely many global sections O_Y^r onto A. Their Koszul complex is locally contractible because, after trivializing A, they generate the unit ideal. It remains exact after tensoring by arbitrary M. Write Reg(t) for H^i(M tensor A^{t-i})=0 for all i>0. Reg(0) is the hypothesis. Twist the Koszul complex by M tensor A^{t+1-i}. Its preceding terms are copies of M tensor A^{t-i-j}. Their H^{i+j} vanish by Reg(t). Successive kernel sequences move H^i of the target to these higher groups and finally to zero. Thus Reg(t+1), and induction gives every t>=0.

Twisting by M tensor A^{t+1}, the obstruction to H^0(M tensor A^t)^r onto H^0(M tensor A^{t+1}) is H^1 of the first kernel. The same kernel sequences kill it through H^j(M tensor A^{t-j})=0. Multiplication therefore surjects in every degree. Every high-degree section is a product of the chosen A-sections with sections of M. Serre generation makes M tensor A^t globally generated for large t. Stalkwise, its generated image is contained in the image of H^0(M) tensor A^t; untwisting proves that H^0(M) generates M.

This proves the complete relative statement and its immediate proof. Serre thresholds may depend on fixed coherent factors, while the choice of ample divisors can remain fixed. GJKM4.6 retains its SMOOTH/projective-over-affine/perfect-field hypotheses. Its reference identifies the issue; its theorem is not applied to singular Y. No fresh whole BS-book reading is asserted.

notes.summary: Repaired finite-perfect-field diagonal descent and Jacobian-corrected BIG subadditivity, for reduced equidimensional finite-type algebras over perfect characteristic-p fields.
notes.detailedSummary: Twisted Frobenius base change and finite-presentation Hom kernels/images give faithful-flat membership descent. No extension-field action on k or test-ideal base-change assumption is used. The infinite-field HH02 dependency remains explicit.
notes.text:
Let R be reduced equidimensional and essentially finite type over perfect k of characteristic p. Set S=R tensor_k R, I=ker(S->R), q=p^e, E=Hom_R(F_*^e R,R), H=Hom_S(F_*^e S,S), Q=Hom_S(F_*^e I,R). The kernel K of H->Q consists exactly of diagonal-compatible maps. Its restriction image in E is the degree-e diagonal module D_e.

Frobenius is finite and all its source modules are finitely presented. For perfect k'/k, the S'-linear base-change isomorphism is F_*s tensor lambda |-> F_*(s tensor lambda^q), with inverse using unique q-th roots. It respects balancing because a F_*s=F_*(a^q s). The same construction applies to I and the quotient R and commutes with their maps. A finite presentation proves flat Hom base change by a matrix-kernel calculation. Flatness preserves the kernels and images defining K and D_e. Thus D_e(R) tensor_k k'=D_e(R'), inside E tensor_k k'=E(R'). Differentials and Fitting ideals commute with field extension, so the Jacobian does also. Perfect-field extension preserves geometric reducedness and equidimensionality here.

For finite k take the infinite perfect k'=perfection(k(t)). The infinite-field theorem gives (x tensor1)(phi tensor1) in D_e(R') for x in Jac and phi in E. Faithful flatness detects membership in E/D_e and proves x phi in D_e(R). This neither defines an L-action on k nor assumes test-ideal base change.

The complete infinite-field immediate source proof uses the disclosed published HH02 Theorem3.4: for x in Jac choose a generically separable polynomial normalization A such that x R^{1/q} lies in the free R-module A^{1/q}[R]=A^{1/q} tensor_A R. Tensor with R^{1/q}; freeness lifts multiplication to R tensor_k R^{1/q}. Compose multiplication by x tensor1, that lift and 1 tensor phi. The maps are R tensor_k R-linear and reduce to x phi. The historical HH02 theorem is explicit background, not a fresh recursive proof.

Finite-presentation Hom–tensor adjunction expresses full Frobenius maps on S as sums of tensor maps. The tensor of the two big test ideals is stable under product-pair maps, so minimality contains the product test ideal of S in it. Diagonal restriction then gives tau(R,D^(2),a^s b^t) subset tau(R,a^s)tau(R,b^t). The restriction hypotheses hold after choosing regular elements f,g in the ideals with regular localizations; perfectness makes their product smooth and its test ideal unit. Clearing denominators gives a regular element in the diagonal image. The diagonal algebra is nondegenerate by lifting a map on regular Frobenius, which is finite projective there, and clearing a power of f tensor f.

Choose a common nonzero big test element. The big Cartier formula expresses tau as sums of phi(F_*c). Multiplication by x in Jac replaces each full map by a diagonal map, including its ideal pre-twist. Therefore Jac tau(R,a^s b^t) subset tau(R,D^(2),a^s b^t) subset tau(R,a^s)tau(R,b^t). All ideals are BIG/nonfinitistic.

For a graded family, power invariance directs tau(b_ell^{m/ell}) under common multiples and quasi-compact Noetherian stabilization supplies its maximal member s_m. Choose ell attaining s_{ml} and iterate the finite-exponent formula. Since tau(b_ell^{m/ell}) subset s_m, Jac^{l-1}s_{ml} subset s_m^l. No uncorrected singular formula is used.

Sources are corrected Smolkin1805.08739v3 Sections2–3 and CEMS1412.6453v4 big conventions. Takagi v2 is a big tilde-tau cross-check, not a finitistic substitution. Old Smolkin3.12/5.15 and too-strong CEMS2.10 are not applied. Kunz, existence of big test elements and HH02 are disclosed historical foundations. notes.summary: Isolated normal affine perfect-charp germs admit actual normal primary common models with Cartier K+Delta; all-support Fekete computes raw Cartier-obstacle envelopes before positivity.
notes.detailedSummary: The construction principalizes every finite primary collection, flattens the canonical module through Fitt1, matches rational sections, and proves actual blowup realization by the punctured graph. Uniform correction bounds use the full fibre, not a nonprimary conductor.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n2. Let B be normal integral affine finite type over perfect characteristic-p k, x CLOSED of codimension>=2, and B minus x regular. Include the primary gauge a in any finite primary collection. Blow up the product and finitely normalize. If a product of nonzero ideals is locally principal (f), each factor has a fractional inverse obtained from the others divided by f. An expression for 1 has a unit summand, which makes the factor principal. Thus every prescribed ideal is principalized. The product defines full-fibre effective Cartier F_0 with ample O(-F_0).

The normal, possibly non-CM model has coherent torsionfree rank-one canonical sheaf. G=Fitt_1(omega) is unit off the fibre. Where G is unit, the module is cyclic; torsionfree rank one over a local domain makes it free. Current Stacks15.27.3–4 therefore makes its strict transform on Bl_G invertible. On each chart R'=R[G/a_0] subset R_{a_0}, Fitt_1 is unit and Fitt_0 vanishes after inverting a_0, hence in R'. Finite normalization preserves the resulting line bundle.

Choose the SAME rational section for this line bundle and the canonical sheaf on the puncture. Only then is K_Y-L_0 fibre-supported. Choose r with rF_0>=K_Y-L_0, and Delta=rF_0-(K_Y-L_0)>=0. Then K_Y+Delta=L_0+rF_0 is Cartier.

The negative Fitting exceptional bundle tensor a sufficiently high O(-F_0) power is ample; finite normalization preserves ampleness. A high power is generated and very ample, written O(-F) with full-fibre F. Hartogs puts J=Gamma(O(-F)) in B. It is coherent, unit off x, proper and primary; generation gives J O_Y=O(-F). Include immersion sections among its generators. Y and Bl_J are integral closed subschemes of the same projective space with the same dense punctured graph, hence are the identical scheme-theoretic graph closure. This proves ACTUAL primary realization, not arbitrary-model cofinality.

Since the puncture is smooth over perfect k, Jac(Y/k) is unit there. Coherence gives J^a O_Y subset Jac for some integer a. Also Delta<=bF and a^{N_J} subset J. Thus on every normalized support 0<=v(Jac)<=a v(J)<=a N_J and v(bF)=b v(J).

For any integral fibre-supported Cartier C, first pass to Frac(B/support(v)); its generic point is on the puncture. Properness gives a centre and a primary denominator remains nonzero. Pull O(C) with its generic trivialization to the valuation ring and set f_C minus the generator value. Actual Cartier bounds by the principalized gauge make it finite; G331 makes it continuous on all supports. No map from Frac(B) to a support quotient is presumed.

For EVERY m>=1 let I_m=Gamma(O(mC)) and b_m=I_m O_Y tensor O(-mC). Hartogs gives an actual ideal in B, unit off x and containing a^{Mm} for a fixed C>=-M E_a. It is unit or primary. The b_m are nonzero actual graded base ideals. At every support u_m=-v(I_m)/m=f_C-v(b_m)/m<=f_C. Subadditivity of v(I_m) gives the ALL-index Fekete limit u=lim_m u_m=sup_m u_m, unchanged along multiples. No monotonicity of this sequence is claimed.

Each u_m is a C competitor. If -v(I)/q<=f_C, every fibre prime divisor of normal Y gives I^r O_Y subset O(rqC); other height-one orders are automatic because I is in B and C vanishes there. Normal height-one intersection gives I^r subset I_{rq}, hence -v(I)/q<=u. Rational approximation with a small negative gauge shift handles every C competitor. For a D competitor, the decreasing compact closed sets {h_alpha>=f_C+epsilon} have empty intersection, so one is empty; h_alpha-epsilon is a C competitor. Let epsilon vanish. Consequently p(f_C)=u on ALL supports BEFORE continuity or positivity has been recognized.

notes.summary: Isolated normal affine finite-type CLOSED codimension>=2 germs over PERFECT charp have continuous geometric envelopes on ALL supports, without smooth models or resolution.

notes.text:
Use G331 and n2–n5. On n5’s actual normal primary Y put H=-F, A=O(H), L=K_Y+Delta Cartier. CEMS v4 big test ideals apply because Y is normal integral, F-finite, separated finite type over perfect k with the stated duality. No anticanonical finite-generation assumption is imposed.

Power invariance is proved without smooth roots. For b nonzero and r>=1, A_e=ceil(qt) and B_e=r ceil(qt/r) satisfy A_e<=B_e<=A_e+r-1. With a common big test element c, one inclusion of tau(Delta,b^t) and tau(Delta,(b^r)^{t/r}) is immediate. For the reverse take nonzero z in b^r; cz is also a test element and cz b^{A_e} subset c b^{B_e}. The tail trace formula proves equality. Gradedness directs tau(Delta,b_ell^{m/ell}) under common multiples; Noetherianity on a finite affine cover gives global stabilization. Denote its maximal member t_m and the zero-boundary version s_m.

Choose c_0 with (c_0-i)H-L ample for i=1..dimY. Fix m and ell attaining t_m; lambda=m/ell. CEMS2.3 gives, for any sufficiently large lower tail index,
t_m=sum_e Image[F_*^e(b_ell^{ceil(lambda q)} O(K_Y-qL-D_0))->O_Y].
The Cartier test divisor D_0 is SCHEME-GLOBAL: on a finite affine cover choose test elements and bounded rounding corrections; an effective Weil E contains their closed zero divisors. For large r, a nonzero section of generated O(-E) tensor A^r, viewed in A^r, has effective Cartier zero divisor D_0>=E. Normal height-one intersection shows its local equations are multiples of the local test elements. Multiples remain test elements, so the affine arbitrary-tail formulas glue. D_0 may depend on m,ell; c_0 does not.

Set a_e=ceil(qm/ell), j_e=ell a_e-qm in[0,ell-1]. Products of global I_ell sections generate b_ell^{a_e} O(a_e ell C). After twisting the trace target by O(mC+c_0H), multiplication by these products INSIDE Frobenius gives a surjection from copies of
Q_{e,j}=F_*^e O(q(c_0H-L)+K_Y-D_0-jC)
onto the trace source. These maps are O-linear since scalar action is by q-th powers; no base factor is incorrectly pulled through Frobenius.

H^i(Q_{e,j} A^{-i}) equals the cohomology of the fixed coherent reflexive O(K_Y-D_0-jC) tensored by the ample q-th power O(q((c_0-i)H-L)). There are finitely many i,j. Serre vanishing and n3 make every sufficiently large Q_{e,j} generated. Trace images are generated and their tail sum stabilizes. Hence t_m O(mC+c_0H) is generated for EVERY m, with fixed c_0. Set c=c_0+1 and tensor once more by A.

Let F_m=t_m O(mC) A^c and J_m=Gamma(F_m). Hartogs puts sections in B; generation gives EXACTLY J_m O_Y=F_m on every support. Before the extra A, the generated sheaf’s sections lie in B, so it is a subsheaf of O_Y. The extra twist puts F_m inside J O_Y and makes J_m proper. T_0=tau(Y,Delta) is unit off the fibre and contains J^r O_Y. A common test element proves b T_0 subset tau(Delta,b): f phi(F_*z)=phi(F_*(f^q z)) for f in b. Thus b_m T_0 subset t_m and I_m J^{r+c} subset J_m. This supplies a primary power. J_m is an ACTUAL primary ideal and
g_m=-v(J_m)/m=f_C-[c v(J)+v(t_m)]/m
is a continuous geometric competitor.

For every l, b_{ml}T_0 subset t_{ml} subset s_{ml}, while n4 gives Jac^{l-1}s_{ml} subset s_m^l. These ideal values are finite on ALL supports because they contain primary powers. Put h=f_C-p(f_C)=lim_l v(b_{ml})/(ml). Reversing containment gives
v(s_m)/m <= [v(b_{ml})+v(T_0)]/(ml)+(l-1)v(Jac)/(ml).
At a fixed support let l tend to infinity: v(s_m)<=m h+v(Jac). Boundary monotonicity and the Cartier shift with 0<=Delta<=bF give O(-bF)s_m subset t_m subset s_m, so v(t_m)<=v(s_m)+b v(J). Therefore
0<=p(f_C)-g_m<=[c v(J)+v(Jac)+b v(J)]/m<=(c+a+b)N_J/m.
The finite T_0 term disappears pointwise before this uniform bound. Individual functions may have infinite values; all correction ideals remain finite. Uniform approximation by actual C profiles recognizes p(f_C) in C. No increasing-D, energy or capacity shortcut is used.

The finite primary collection was arbitrary. Signed rational obstacles are carried on these models; denominator clearing and positive homogeneity apply. N2’s density and nonexpansivity prove CE for EVERY finite continuous obstacle. N2 then supplies bounded USC greatest minorants from ONE decreasing C-net and the exact primary-gauge cocycle.

notes.detailedSummary: Surface all-characteristic, isolated char0, general finite-Q open-locus, exact BFJ, fixed-model/SM and energy diagnostics retain their precise restrictions. Neither alterations nor failed nonprimary bounds become normal counterexamples.
notes.text:
Use G331/B341/E350 and n2–n6. The complete paper reconstructs all ten 376 proof bodies, separately from their differing actual FINAL objects; none is a grant.

For an excellent normal surface in ANY characteristic/residue field, normalize a finite product-primary blowup. Its finite singular locus and normal completions satisfy current Stacks54.14.5 condition(4), giving a regular common projective model T by normalized blowups. Normal Stein factorization gives Gamma(T,O)=R and connected full fibre. Write a O_T=O(-sum b_i E_i), b_i>0. Regularity makes every fibre curve Cartier. The residue-weighted intersection matrix M is symmetric, off-diagonal nonnegative and connected, with Mb<=0 and a strict coordinate from the original ample tautological bundle. For A=-M, t_i=b_i z_i,
t^t A t=sum_i(Ab)_i b_i z_i^2+sum_{i<j}(-A_ij)b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2.
It is positive definite. Principal inverse matrices are nonnegative: a nonzero negative part of A_J x=y>=0 gives x_-^t y<0. Thus integer d_i>0 with Md<0 exist. Positive fibre degrees give an ample FULL-fibre negative Cartier boundary; high-power generation and the punctured graph make T an ACTUAL primary blowup.

For a regular refinement, push down a negative nef D' to Cartier D. Projection gives D.E_i>=0. The exceptional difference F=D'-mu^*D satisfies M_J f>=0, hence f<=0 and h_{D'}<=h_D on all supports. Uniform core approximation, then an actual decreasing net, controls every bounded D competitor by its finite trace c_i=b_i h(ord_Ei/b_i), with c<=0 and Mc>=0. For a model obstacle, the compact polytope -Bb_i<=c_i<=min(0,b_i f(nu_i)), Mc>=0 is closed under coordinatewise maximum. Its greatest vector is a geometric Cartier competitor dominating EVERY D competitor. Signed density gives all-continuous CE. This is a surface argument, not higher-dimensional pushdown.

For CLOSED normal algebraic germs over algclosed CHAR0, use the THREE-author published BdFF source. Uniform geometric core limits enter the source-nef cone through Lemma1.12 with FIXED base trace zero; no converse is asserted. Its largest trace envelope W for a signed obstacle has MZ(a)<=W<=C and W<=0. In the isolated case, clear denominators before integral4.11. It gives primary upper approximants B_k>=W converging coefficientwise, with zero/unit separately handled. Finite determining errors eta_k->0 give B_k+eta_k Z(a)<=W<=B_k. Continuous profiles are uniformly Cauchy on divisors and therefore all supports. ONE continuous majorant of any D competitor at the finite vertices is source-controlled by W, proving that the uniform C limit is the raw envelope.

For general nonisolated char0 use3.17, not4.11. Q=d(K)Jac may be nonprimary. Graded section ideals are actual unit/primary; multiplier ideals b_k may not be. Primary truncations b'_k=b_k+a^{A_0 k} yield U_k>=W+Z(Q)/(Nk) and coefficient convergence. Finite trace errors give U_k+eta_k Z(a)<=W. On divisors, W-v(Q)/(Nk)<=u_k<=W+eta_k. Extend continuous DIFFERENCES first on OPEN O={v(Q)<infinity}; only then restrict to compact K_L. They converge uniformly on K_L and locally uniformly on O. The same one-majorant finite-vertex argument identifies the limit with the raw envelope on O. Infinite-Q supports remain unresolved. The criterion v(I) uniformly bounded on all points, equivalently all centred divisors, iff I is unit/primary follows by a primary-power bound or a positive-dimensional quotient killing a nonprimary ideal, then divisorial density in {v(I)>L}.

Exact BFJ specialization remains smooth affine CLOSED algclosed CHAR0, with direct DVR/empty cases. Substantive closed-face continuity and EVERY retraction are retained. Full3.18/3.22 gives W_j<=W<=j W_j/(j+C_0); for -M<=W its error is <=MC_0/j on all retractions and supports. No global thinness or mere interior-convexity substitute is used.

For a finite reduced cover A->B of an excellent NORMAL target, require EVERY minimal source component to dominate. Pull a source function to generic normal closures. G331’s coefficient trace has FULL fibre support, including inseparable and quotient supports; on a normal closure the fibre is a finite orbit. Finite maxima of conjugate pullbacks descend positively. Thus M(h)(v)=max_{rho(w)=v}h(w) preserves C. Finite fibre maximum commutes with actual decreasing C-nets, preserving D. Pullbacks and maxima prove p_B(rho^*f)=rho^*p_A(f). An ACTUAL source with CE gives target CE by compact quotient topology; no alteration or universal-cover theorem is substituted.

Apply this to A=k[U,V,W,z_1,...,z_r]/(UW-V^2), B=k[s,t,z_1,...,z_r], U=s^2,V=st,W=t^2, at the origins. A is a hypersurface domain, S2 and regular off codimension two, hence normal in EVERY characteristic. The cover is finite of generic degree two, purely inseparable in characteristic two. Its closed fibre has basis 1,s,t and length three, so it is nonflat. The source is regular and satisfies n6 over EVERY perfect characteristic-p field; in algclosed char0 it satisfies exact BFJ. Hence these nonisolated targets for r>=1 have GLOBAL CE in all those cases. This is a new explicit family, not a universal nonisolated theorem.

376’s fixed ACTUAL smooth-primary-model theorem and fully quantified SM condition retain their scopes.
